headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API/file surfaces interacting with plane’s broad networked task workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, while plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other, especially if an orchestrator forwards outputs without provenance checks. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal output is forwarded into plane task text or comments without sanitization
IF plane file uploads are parsed as instructions by an upstream agent
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding between agents
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages
Strip executable-looking markup from OpenBBTerminal outputs
Require manual review before plane ingests OpenBBTerminal content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and plane handles files, notes, and hyperlinks with broad network egress. If OpenBBTerminal content is copied into plane or plane uploads are sent onward, sensitive financial or licensed material can leak across the pair. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, so this is inferred but still plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal data is pasted or uploaded into plane
IF plane forwards uploaded files or notes to external services
mitigations: Restrict cross-posting of financial data
Use separate workspaces for each agent
Block uploads containing licensed or confidential data
Review outbound network destinations for plane

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and multiple instances; plane supports multiple instances and broad network egress, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same filesystem or git state. Without a shared mutable resource, direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the orchestration layer is not described, so I avoid none but keep it low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend or shared API token
IF an orchestrator grants both write access to one shared resource
mitigations: Assign separate credentials per agent
Avoid shared mutable workspaces
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Audit for overlapping API scopes

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can emit financial analysis through APIs and MCP, and plane is an issue/task system that may store or route that output. If plane treats OpenBBTerminal output as authoritative, errors can cascade into task creation or scheduling decisions. The profiles do not prove automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high, but the pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF plane uses OpenBBTerminal output as a source of truth without verification
IF downstream tasks or schedules are created from unreviewed financial analysis
mitigations: Require human verification before task creation
Attach source links to every imported analysis
Add confidence thresholds for automated ingestion
Log and review all agent-to-agent transformations

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while plane stores files, notes, and issue content with self-hosted deployment available. If regulated financial or licensed data is moved into plane, retention, residency, or access-control mismatches can create compliance gaps. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the risk is inferred and medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in plane
IF plane retention or access controls differ from OpenBBTerminal handling
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of plane
Set explicit retention limits
Review self-hosted access controls
Document data-class handling rules
